snippet.text: At `low`, Melian's own lenses finish fast and find little. Example: re-reviews of three merged pull requests, [#613](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/pull/613), [#619](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/pull/619) and [#623](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/pull/623), were scored against the 23 real defects they held. At `low`, most lenses finished in under 30 seconds, and four runs found none of #619's 7 defects.

snippet.text: Lens generation and compaction use the scrutiny level's tier; escalation moves to its next tier's thinking. Failover models retain the serving tier's level. Verification uses verifier thinking even when its models fall back to lens routes. Walkthroughs use light thinking, under their existing revision cache and rerun rules. Direct triage uses the selected lens tier's level through pi-ai's simple completion API when explicit, retaining raw completion when unset. The reserved decision tier has no new adapter. Lens selection, including escalation, verifier candidate identity and triage identity distinguish explicit levels. Telemetry's requested field records them; sent settings still come from provider bodies. Live evals accept per-run `MELIAN_EVAL_THINKING="heavy=medium,verifier=high"` after model overrides, and their spend lines print recorded levels. A live eval fills a thinking-only golden tier with its supplied model and retains the tier’s configured thinking. Replacing the verifier model retains its configured thinking when the per-run override leaves that tier out. Triage measurement format 3 stores and renders the light tier’s effective level. Comparison refuses different levels; older absent levels remain a distinct unset value and compare with each other. [The measurement rule](decisions/2026-10-19-triage-thinking-identity.md) records compatibility. The committed routes set `thinking: low` on the heavy tier and on a light route that copied medium's model, which gives triage its model and level. The verifier level stays unset. trigger.snippet: Lens generation and compaction use the scrutiny level's tier; escalation moves to its next tier's thinking. Failover models retain the serving tier's level. Verification uses verifier thinking even when its models fall back to lens routes. Walkthroughs use light thinking, under their existing revision cache and rerun rules. Direct triage uses the selected lens tier's level through pi-ai's simple completion API when explicit, retaining raw completion when unset. The reserved decision tier has no new adapter. Lens selection, including escalation, verifier candidate identity and triage identity distinguish explicit levels. Telemetry's requested field records them; sent settings still come from provider bodies. Live evals accept per-run `MELIAN_EVAL_THINKING="heavy=medium,verifier=high"` after model overrides, and their spend lines print recorded levels. A live eval fills a thinking-only golden tier with its supplied model and retains the tier’s configured thinking. Replacing the verifier model retains its configured thinking when the per-run override leaves that tier out. Triage measurement format 3 stores and renders the light tier’s effective level. Comparison refuses different levels; older absent levels remain a distinct unset value and compare with each other. [The measurement rule](decisions/2026-10-19-triage-thinking-identity.md) records compatibility. The committed routes set `thinking: low` on the heavy tier and on a light route that copied medium's model, which gives triage its model and level. The verifier level stays unset. From 2026-10-24 the design lens ran on Sol 5.6 at `high` by taking the medium tier to itself, and from step 37 it runs there on its own route, `lenses.design.route`, while medium returns to Terra; [the route decision](decisions/2026-10-24-design-lens-on-codex-route.md) records the trade and [the lens-route decision](decisions/2026-11-08-lens-routes.md) the rule. [The low-reasoning decision](decisions/2026-10-19-reasoning-low-for-heavy-and-triage.md) records the measurements and its consequence for the walkthrough. From 2026-11-27 the heavy, medium and light tiers all run at `high`, which raised recall on three re-reviewed pull requests from 24% to 39% for about 60% more cost; [the high-thinking decision](decisions/2026-11-27-melians-own-routes-run-at-high-thinking.md) records the measurement. [The tier reasoning decision](decisions/2026-10-19-tier-thinking-routes.md) records the contract and reopen versions.
